required_interface_contract.physical_adapter: A concrete B1.10 implementation of canonical_physical_model_t that advances the real physical model over generic [t0,t1] without file I/O or integer-day projection.
required_interface_contract.committed_state: A concrete continuation state whose clone/checkpoint contains all and only physical continuation state required for deterministic replay; worker scratch and reconstructible solver workspace remain excluded.
required_interface_contract.forcing: A canonical forcing object sufficient for the short continuation interval and independent of legacy file parsing.
required_interface_contract.result: The accepted endpoint and diagnostics must be attributable to the requested interval and replayable from the same committed state.
required_interface_contract.mass: The real physical seam must expose complete unrounded accepted-interval storage and signed external boundary accounting sufficient to enforce the hard mass gate and construct the F-MQ event fixture without rounded legacy reports.
required_interface_contract.transactionality: Rejected trials and incomplete requested intervals must never alter the externally committed physical state; successful completion commits exactly once.
required_interface_contract.time: The real physical path must accept generic non-midnight, non-day [t0,t1] intervals.

unblock_conditions: F-CI/F-KT materializes and qualifies a concrete B1.10 physical adapter on the canonical integration line.
A qualified real B1.10 committed continuation checkpoint can be captured without persisting worker scratch.
A short generic physical continuation can be run from that checkpoint and deterministically replayed.
The accepted interval returns complete unrounded mass accounting sufficient for the F-MQ hard mass gate.
F-MQ04b can generate a reference-run record from the exact canonical commit and F-MQ04c admits it into the F-MQ03 fixture builder.
